access for inference of foundation models\\n\\nTo prevent a user from invoking foundation models, you need to deny access to API actions\\nthat invoke models directly. The following example shows a identity-based policy that denies\\naccess to running inference on a specific model. This policy can be used as a service control policy (SCP) to control model access across an organization.\\n\\n#### Using JSON\\n\\n#### Using\\n\\n```\\n{\\n \\\"Version\\\":\\\"2012-10-17\\\",\\n \\\"Statement\\\": {\\n \\\"Sid\\\": \\\"DenyInference\\\",\\n \\\"Effect\\\": \\\"Deny\\\",\\n \\\"Action\\\": [\\n \\\"bedrock:InvokeModel\\\",\\n \\\"bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream\\\",\\n \\\"bedrock:CreateModelInvocationJob\\\"\\n ],\\n \\\"Resource\\\": \\\"arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/model-id\\\"\\n }\\n }\\n\\n```\\n\\nTo deny inference access to all foundation models, use `*` for the model ID.\\nOther actions, such as `Converse` and `StartAsyncInvoke`, are blocked\\nautomatically when `InvokeModel` is denied. If you want to explicitly deny all inference actions, you can use `bedrock:InvokeModel*` as a wildcard or add `bedrock:Converse` and `bedrock:ConverseStream` to the action list. For a list of model IDs, see Supported foundation models in Amazon Bedrock\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/security_iam_id-based-policy-examples.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"How do I resolve \\\"Access denied\\\" errors when I try to invoke serverless foundation models in Amazon Bedrock?\",\"context\":\"### Activate models at your AWS Account level\\n\\nTo activate models at your AWS Account level, take the following actions:\\n\\n* Make sure that you are an administrator with\u00a0[AWS Marketplace permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-access.html#model-access-permissions).\\n* Run the [InvokeModel](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_InvokeModel.html) or [InvokeModelWithResponseStream](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_InvokeModelWithResponseStream.html) API call with the model that you require. Or, run the [ListFoundationModelAgreementOffers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_ListFoundationModelAgreementOffers.html) and [CreateFoundationModelAgreement](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_CreateFoundationModelAgreement.html) API calls.\\n\\nAfter your administrator activates the AWS Marketplace models, make sure that the IAM users or roles have the required permissions to invoke the models.\\n\\nExample IAM policy that allows the invocation of a model with an inference profile:\\n\\n```plaintext\\n{\\n \\\"Version\\\": \\\"2012-10-17\\\",\\n \\\"Statement\\\": [\\n {\\n \\\"Sid\\\": \\\"AllowMarketplaceModelInvocation\\\",\\n \\\"Effect\\\": \\\"Allow\\\",\\n \\\"Action\\\": [\\n \\\"bedrock:InvokeModel\\\",\\n \\\"bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream\\\"\\n ],\\n \\\"Resource\\\": [\\n \\\"arn:aws:bedrock:*::inference-profile/replace-inference-profile-id\\\",\\n \\\"arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/replace-foundation-model-id\\\"\\n ]\\n }\\n ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**Note:** Replace **your-inference-profile-id** with your inference profile ID and **your-foundation-model-id** with your foundation model ID\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-serverless-models-access-denied\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up Bedrock AccessDeniedException troubleshooting docs"}

{"id": "0c0ecd76-22f4-4759-bae1-77b70b359238", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "It might be your IAM policy, but it often isn't. The exact error message usually tells you which cause it is.

**Fixable in your IAM policy**
- The calling role or user lacks `bedrock:InvokeModel` (or `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream`) on the right resources. The message usually reads "...is not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel on resource: ...".
- The resource ARN in the policy doesn't match what you call. If you use a cross-Region inference profile, the policy needs both the `inference-profile/...` ARN and the `foundation-model/...` ARN in every Region the profile can route to. This is a very common cause.
- A permissions boundary or session policy on the role is limiting access.

**Coming from somewhere else**
- **An SCP in AWS Organizations.** The message usually says "explicit deny in a service control policy". This is common with Region-restricting SCPs and cross-Region inference profiles. The fix is in the SCP, not your role's policy.
- **Model access isn't activated in the account.** This applies to serverless and Marketplace models. Someone with AWS Marketplace permissions has to enable the model, either by invoking it once or through the foundation model agreement APIs. After that, your role also needs permission to invoke it.
- **A VPC endpoint policy.** If your app reaches Bedrock through an interface endpoint, the endpoint's policy can deny the call.
- **Calling the wrong model ID or Region.** The model may not be available or enabled in that Region, and this can also show up as `AccessDeniedException` or `ValidationException`.

**Quick triage**
1. Read the full error text. "explicit deny in a service control policy" or "explicit deny in an identity-based policy" points straight at the source. "No identity-based policy allows..." means your role is missing the permission.
2. Compare the model ID, inference profile, and Region in your call with the resources in your policy.
3. Check whether the account is in an Organization and whether any SCPs touch Bedrock or restrict Regions.

If you send me the role name, the model ID or inference profile, the Region, and the full error message, I can check the role's policies and attached boundaries in your account and work out which cause it is. Docs for reference: [Troubleshooting InvokeModel API errors](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-invokemodel-api-error) and [AccessDenied with cross-Region inference profiles in Organizations](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-access-denied-exception).", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
